facts.text: Random or probability-weighted sampling supports straightforward estimates of real operational performance when the sampling population and probabilities represent intended operation.
facts.quote: Random or probability-weighted sampling is the method that supports straightforward estimates of real operational performance, provided the sampling population and probabilities represent intended operation.

facts.text: Stratification is usually preferable for operational-performance sampling: ensure enough samples from important machine, site and weather strata, then weight the strata back to their operational prevalence.
facts.quote: Stratification is usually preferable: deliberately ensure enough samples from important machine, site and weather strata, then weight the strata back to their operational prevalence.

facts.text: Random, stratified and probability-weighted sampling can support unbiased estimates of detection and false-alarm rates for the assumed scenario distribution, with classical confidence intervals.
facts.quote: Can claim: unbiased estimates of detection and false-alarm rates for the assumed scenario distribution, with classical confidence intervals

facts.text: Stratified sampling can support per-stratum performance claims.
facts.quote: per-stratum claims and lower variance with stratification.

facts.text: Stratified sampling can reduce the variance of performance estimates.
Performance claims from random, stratified or probability-weighted sampling are not valid if the assumed scenario distribution is wrong.
facts.quote: Cannot claim: anything valid if the distribution is wrong.

facts.text: Pure Monte Carlo sampling is extremely inefficient for rare dangerous events; the rare-event limitation is documented in peer-reviewed accelerated-evaluation literature.
facts.quote: Pure Monte Carlo is extremely inefficient for rare dangerous events; the rare-event limitation is documented in the peer-reviewed accelerated-evaluation literature [34].
